title: The Afternoon Brief: Ownership shifts and injury reports define a quiet Tuesday
dek: Liverpool's ownership changed hands, Mourinho took the podium at Real Madrid, and the day's injury reports on Swanson, Tyson, and Hall filled out rosters across baseball and football.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: The biggest movement today was in ownership and leadership, not on the field: Liverpool's new investors, Michigan State's new athletic director, and Mourinho's Real Madrid unveiling all point to structural change, while injury updates across MLB and the NFL add up to a day of accounting rather than action.
bottom_line: Tuesday's news centered on ownership and leadership transitions rather than results: a new investor group took a near-40-percent stake in Liverpool, Mourinho was formally unveiled at Real Madrid, and Michigan State moved to finalize a new athletic director. Alongside that, three separate injury reports, for the Cubs' Dansby Swanson, the Saints' Jordyn Tyson, and the Jets' Breece Hall, filled out the day's roster news without changing any competitive outcome yet. The LIV Golf financial story deepened, with a vendor now claiming more than $1.1 million owed and termination notices going out to contractors as the league seeks new funding. The honest read is that today's reporting establishes new ownership and personnel facts clearly, while LIV's financial trajectory and several injury timelines remain open questions. Watch for regulatory sign-off on the Liverpool deal, Michigan State's official hire announcement, and whether BC Partners' funding for LIV closes before vendor disputes escalate further.
body: The day's clearest thread is transition. A new ownership group has taken a substantial stake in Liverpool FC, a new manager was formally presented at Real Madrid, and a new athletic director is being installed at Michigan State. None of these changes were sudden; each had been building, and today marked the point where they became official or newly confirmed.

The Liverpool deal is the largest of these. A consortium called 1892 Holdings, led by Amit Bhatia and including Jeff Bezos and Eduardo Saverin, has acquired close to 38 percent of the club from Fenway Sports Group, in a deal that values Liverpool between 5 billion and 6 billion pounds. Bhatia is set to become vice-chairman pending regulatory approval, and the consortium holds an option to acquire a controlling stake within 12 months. At Real Madrid, José Mourinho was officially unveiled as manager on a three-year contract, his first spell in charge of the club since 2013; he opens the season away at Espanyol on Saturday with six new signings integrated into the squad. Michigan State is finalizing the hire of Dan Bartholomae, currently Western Michigan's athletic director, to fill the vacancy left by J Batt's departure to Kentucky.

On the injury side, three separate updates came in from different sports. Cubs shortstop Dansby Swanson has a Grade 2 oblique strain and is expected to miss four to six weeks, a window that could end his regular season as Chicago defends its wild-card position. Saints rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson suffered a right hamstring injury in Thursday's joint practice with Jacksonville and could be out roughly two months, a timeline that would keep him sidelined at least into Week 6. Jets running back Breece Hall strained his right groin Monday and is expected to miss two to three weeks, though coach Aaron Glenn said he is expected to be ready for the Sept. 13 opener against Tennessee.

The LIV Golf story carries forward from this morning with more detail. Vendors and contractors report unpaid invoices ranging from thousands of dollars to nearly $100,000, and one supplier, Mobii Systems Group, claims it is owed more than $1.1 million. The league has issued 30-day termination notices to some contractors and filed a WARN Act notice, even as full-time employees have not reported missed paychecks. LIV is pursuing a funding deal with BC Partners' credit division as the Saudi PIF's support ends this month.

Elsewhere, the AFL Tribunal upheld Jacob van Rooyen's three-match ban for a strike on Port Adelaide's Aliir Aliir, rejecting Melbourne's appeal and its biomechanist evidence. The Premier League announced it will publish full Key Match Incidents Panel verdicts on referee and VAR calls for the first time this season. The Scottish FA joined England, Wales, and the Republic of Ireland in withdrawing support for Gianni Infantino's 2027 FIFA re-election bid, aligning with UEFA's 55 member associations. Scottie Scheffler's eight-shot FedEx St. Jude win, reported this morning, stands as the day's most decisive competitive result. The desk also reported the deaths of two significant figures: O.J. Brigance, the Ravens' longtime player engagement adviser, at 56 after a 19-year ALS battle, and Bill Rasmussen, ESPN's founder, at 93.

The reporting does not say what prompted LIV's silence toward vendors specifically, beyond the funding timeline, nor does it specify a hard deadline for the BC Partners deal to close. Similarly, the Cubs and Saints have not issued updated statements beyond the initial recovery windows reported by ESPN and NFL Network.

What to watch in the coming days: official confirmation from Michigan State on Bartholomae's hire and contract terms; any court filings from Mobii or other LIV vendors, and whether the BC Partners deal closes before further claims surface; regulatory approval for the Liverpool ownership stake and any move toward the consortium's 12-month option; medical updates on Swanson, Tyson, and Hall as their recovery windows progress, with Hall's status ahead of the Sept. 13 opener a near-term marker; and how FIFA's governance committee responds to the challenge to Infantino's eligibility to run in 2027.
